title: Chicken drumstick, baked or broiled, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken drumsticks are the meat from the lower leg of a chicken, commonly prepared by baking or broiling. In this version the skin is not eaten and the product is pre‑cooked (code 804). The meat is tender, provides high‑quality protein, B‑vitamins and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken drumsticks are a staple in many cuisines, from American BBQ to Asian soups.
Baking without skin reduces fat content while retaining juiciness from the meat’s natural juices.
Poultry is one of the most affordable complete protein sources.
Drumsticks are rich in collagen, beneficial for skin and joint health.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 20 g of complete protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains niacin (B3), vitamin B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for bone health, immunity and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Low fat when skin‑less
items.content: Removing the skin cuts saturated fat, making the dish more heart‑friendly.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: Protein and a modest amount of fat help keep you feeling full longer, useful for weight management.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Insufficient heating can leave salmonella or campylobacter; ensure the product is thoroughly heated.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Pre‑cooked items may contain added salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Some ready‑made products include preservatives or flavor enhancers that may not suit everyone.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reheat drumsticks in the oven, microwave or skillet. They work well added to salads, soups, rice or pasta dishes, and can be enjoyed as a protein‑rich snack. Remove the skin before eating.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the pre‑cooked product refrigerated at 0 °C–4 °C for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight container for 2‑3 months. Ensure it is fully reheated before consumption.
